prompt: An alarm is set to 3 of 5 with a 60-second period. What has to happen for it to fire?

choices.text: Five breaching minutes in a row
choices.why: That is 5 of 5, which misses an outage that flickers.

choices.text: Three breaching minutes in a row
choices.why: The three can be anywhere in the window of five.

choices.text: Any three of the last five minutes
choices.why: Right. They need not be in a row.

choices.text: One breaching minute, held for three
choices.why: Each minute is its own data point; nothing is held.

prompt: An alarm stays in `ALARM` for an hour. How many notifications does its topic receive, counting its return to `OK`?
hint: Alarms notify on a change of state.

choices.why: Periods in the same state notify nothing.
Right. One message entering ALARM and one returning to OK: one per change of state.
The OK action also fires when it returns, if configured, as here.
CloudWatch has no acknowledgement; that belongs to a paging service.

prompt: Besides OK and ALARM, the third state of an alarm, when the data it needs is not there, is ___.
hint: Two words joined by an underscore, in capitals.

prompt: In the model, the API stopped publishing and the `notBreaching` alarm returned to `OK` two minutes later. Why?
hint: What did the empty minutes count as?

choices.text: Its empty minutes counted as good minutes
choices.why: Right. notBreaching turned the silence into good minutes, leaving two bad ones in the window.

choices.text: The errors stopped, so the service recovered
choices.why: No data arrived at all; nothing recovered.

choices.text: CloudWatch resets alarms after five minutes
choices.why: No reset exists; the window simply moved over empty minutes.
Thresholds never move by themselves.

prompt: Errors are published by the application itself. Which missing-data treatment keeps the alarm on when the application crashes?

choices.why: It counts the silence as good, as the model showed.
It leaves the silent minutes out, and the remaining two do not reach three.

choices.text: Any of them, as long as M is 1
choices.why: M of 1 pages on every blip and still loses the crash under notBreaching.
Right. Silence counts as bad, so the alarm stays in ALARM.

hint: Good, bad, left out, or no change.

prompt: Why should alarms name a topic rather than a person's email?

choices.why: A topic delivers to email; that is not the reason.

choices.text: A topic is cheaper than an email
choices.why: Cost is not the point; changing who is paged is.
Alarm actions take ARNs; the topic is how email is reached.
Right. The subscriptions change; forty alarms do not.

prompt: On AWS, what is `set-alarm-state` useful for?
hint: It changes the state until the next evaluation.

choices.text: Silencing an alarm during a deployment
choices.why: The next evaluation sets the real state again within a period.

choices.text: Changing the threshold without a new alarm
choices.why: The threshold is changed with put-metric-alarm.

choices.text: Testing that a page reaches the right phone
choices.why: Right. It runs the actions without breaking anything.
moto changed the state and ran no action at all.

prompt: Which field of an alarm's message tells the person paged why it fired?
hint: CloudWatch's own sentence about the data points.

choices.why: Right. Here: 3 out of the last 5 datapoints were greater than 10.
It says which alarm, not why.
It says where, not why.
It says the state before, not the reason for the change.

prompt: The shop has alarms on errors, latency, queue depth and database CPU. Which should page a person directly?

choices.text: All four, so nothing is missed
choices.why: Four pages for one problem, and no way to tell cause from consequence.

choices.text: Queue depth and CPU, because they come first
choices.why: They may come first and matter only if customers feel them.
A composite pages too; it decides when.
Right. Errors and latency page; causes go on the dashboard and in the message.

prompt: Which composite rule pages on errors at once, and on latency only outside deployments?
hint: NOT applies to the deployment alarm.

choices.why: Right. Errors alone page; latency pages unless a deploy is running.
This needs both at once, so errors alone never page.
That fires whenever no deployment runs, which is nearly always.
Latency would page during every canary.
